page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Daldsv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a local 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and gzip compression placing in the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU metrics and Redis SET operations scoring in the average range. Cryptographic and vector instruction capabilities are supported via AVX-512 and VAES flags, contributing to strong PassMark CPU encryption and extended instruction scores. Memory bandwidth remains average, measuring 107.09 GB/sec for large block reads.

From a resource allocation perspective, this server offers a high-compute, low-memory profile. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a cost-efficient choice for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, avoiding the premium associated with memory-optimized instances. However, the low memory density represents a clear tradeoff, potentially limiting its suitability for large in-memory databases. The inclusion of a fast 1890 GB local NVMe SSD offsets this by providing high-speed local scratch space.

The D32alds_v7 is suited for compute-intensive tasks, single-threaded applications requiring high clock speeds, web serving, and moderate database operations. It is also capable of handling small-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by top-tier text generation speeds on smaller models, though performance scales down to average on larger 7B models due to memory constraints.
